children: Warrior Met Coal reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $507.9 million, up 54.6% from $328.6 million a year earlier, as higher coal sales volume and average selling prices contributed to growth. Net income rose to $49.3 million from $36.6 million, while diluted EPS increased to $0.93 from $0.7.
Revenue was $507.9M, compared with $328.6M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 54.6%.
Net income was $49.3M, compared with $36.6M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 34.7%.
Diluted EPS was $0.93, compared with $0.70 in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 32.9%.
Nine-month coal sales rose 60.8% to $1.45 billion, supported by a 50.4% increase in sales volume and a 7.0% increase in average selling price.
Blue Creek longwall operations began eight months ahead of schedule, contributing to a 45.3% increase in nine-month coal output. Construction was completed in the first quarter of 2026.
Asia accounted for 55% of nine-month sales volume, compared with 44% a year earlier; Europe’s share declined to 32% from 39%.
Nine-month cash cost of sales per ton fell 6.4%, supported by Blue Creek’s lower-cost production and higher volumes.

Met coal prices strengthened in the third quarter amid Chinese supply constraints before softening late in the period. Expected mine restarts and a recovery in Mongolian exports could ease supply conditions.
